title: The For Loop
description: Repeat an action many times without writing it out again and again.

content.value: Imagine you had to write 'I will not throw paper airplanes' 100 times. That would take a long time by hand. A computer can do it instantly. A loop lets you repeat an action as many times as you want, using just a couple of lines.
The most common loop is the `for` loop. You use it together with `range()`, which tells the loop how many times to repeat.
For example, to print 'Hello!' three times:

Notice the space before `print`. That's called indentation. In Python, you press Tab (or a few spaces) to push a line inward. The indented lines are the ones that get repeated. Indentation is how Python knows which lines belong inside the loop.
If you forget to indent the line inside the loop, Python gives an error, because it can't tell what you want to repeat.
The `i` in the loop keeps track of which repeat you're on. It starts counting at 0, so the values go 0, 1, 2, and so on.

for i in range(5):
    print("Repeat number:", i)

editorCode:
for i in range(5):
    print("I am learning so fast!")

quiz.question: What does a loop do?
options: It repeats an action over and over.
It makes the computer shut down.
quiz.explain: A loop repeats the same action again and again, so you don't have to copy and paste the code.

quiz.question: Why do we indent the line inside a loop?
options: To make the code look pretty.
To tell Python which line should be repeated.
quiz.explain: The indentation tells Python exactly which lines belong inside the loop and should be repeated.
